steps.title: The tilted Earth
steps.say: The Earth orbits the Sun with its axis tilted 23.5°, and the axis always points the same way in space.

steps.title: Northern winter
steps.say: In December the northern hemisphere leans away from the Sun, so sunlight hits it at a low angle and spreads out. Days are short and it is winter.

steps.title: Spring
steps.say: A quarter of a year later, neither hemisphere leans toward the Sun. The Sun is overhead at the equator and day and night are about equal.

steps.title: Northern summer
steps.say: In June the northern hemisphere leans toward the Sun. Light hits it more directly and days are long, so it is summer there, while the south has winter.

steps.title: Autumn
steps.say: By September the tilt is sideways to the Sun again. The Sun is overhead at the equator, and the north cools into autumn.

steps.title: Quiz
steps.say: It is not distance from the Sun but tilt that causes seasons. Drag the Earth to where it is summer in the south.
